# Plan: swappable processes (modules) in the Odin MONICA

Goal: make MONICA's processes swappable at runtime, in the main branch. A process (first: soil
temperature, then evapotranspiration) can be computed by:

* **MONICA's own implementation**: today's code, the default;
* a **Crop2ML module**: Odin code generated by PyCrop2ML (the AMEI soil temperature and
  evapotranspiration models);
* a **hand-written variant**: e.g. a PhD student's experimental version of a process.

The C++ AMEI branch needed its own branch because C++ MONICA has no module support. Here the
module support goes into the main branch, so AMEI needs no fork.

Each non-default module can run in three modes:

1. **standalone**: the module runs from a file of inputs, without MONICA;
2. **MONICA as driver**: MONICA supplies the inputs, the module's results are only reported;
3. **integrated**: the module replaces MONICA's own implementation, and its results feed the
   rest of the model.

## Hard requirements

* **R1 Off by default, byte-identical.** With nothing configured, MONICA runs exactly the code it
  runs today, and `odin/tests/diff_outputs.sh` stays byte-identical. This is the gate for every
  merge into main.
* **R2 No noticeable cost.** Moving a process behind the module mechanism must not slow MONICA
  down measurably, in the default configuration nor when MONICA's own implementation is selected
  explicitly.
* **R3 Cheap to extend.** A new variant of a process is one Odin package plus one entry in the
  union and one row in the name table. No other files change.

Related: `odin/CONVENTIONS.md` (rules for Odin code here), `plan-reflective-outputs.md`
(path-based outputs), `plan-serde.md` (saving state), the C++ AMEI branch (`monica_amei`, branch
`amei`, `plan-amei-integration.md`; frozen, reference only), and in PyCrop2ML
`doc/odin-target.md` and `plan-odin-target.md`.

---

## 0. Starting point

### The processes are nearly modules already

The port replaced the C++ back-pointers with explicit parameters, e.g.

```odin
soil_temperature_step(&model.soil_temperature, tmin, tmax, globrad, soil_coverage,
                      snow_depth, temperature_under_snow)
```

in `monica_model_general_step` (`odin/monica/core/monica_model.odin`). That parameter list *is*
the interface of the process. The module mechanism wraps the existing call; it doesn't need to
redesign it.

### PyCrop2ML's Odin target (done)

`cyml -p <package> odin` generates one Odin package per Crop2ML package:

* `<Comp>_State`, `_Rate`, `_Auxiliary` and `_Exogenous` structs with `destroy_*` procs;
* one struct per ModelUnit (its parameters) with `make_*` (defaults), `destroy_*`, `*_init` and
  `*_calculate_model`;
* a Component struct holding the ModelUnits, with setters for the composition parameters and
  `*_init` / `*_calculate_model` procs.

All 12 AMEI packages pass `odin check -vet`. Run for 30 steps, the results equal those of the
generated Python code (bit-identical, or within 1e-12 for DSSAT_EPICST and ApsimCampbell),
except BiomaSurfacePartonSoilSWATHourlyPartonC, which can't run on any target (B9 in
`plan-odin-target.md`).

### The C++ AMEI branch (reference, not to copy)

* One adapter per module (`src/modules/<process>/<Model>_monica_interface.{h,cpp}`, deriving
  from `monica::Run`), owning the generated Component and its five structs.
* Selection by name in sim.json (`SoilTempModel`, `EvapotranspirationModel`), dispatched by an
  if/else chain in `monica-model.cpp` (from line 103).
* "MONICA as driver" is a compile-time switch (`AMEI_SENSITIVITY_ANALYSIS`) and takes extra
  inputs from `simPs.customData` and spare climate columns (`x1`…`x6`).
* Outputs are per-module ids in `build-output.cpp` that dereference the adapter without a null
  check.

Carries over: adapters as the only code that knows both MONICA and a module; selection by name.
Doesn't: the compile-time mode, implicit inputs, per-module output ids, repeated input code.

---

## 1. Design

### 1.1 One union per process, MONICA's own implementation as its default

```odin
Soil_Temperature_Impl :: union #no_nil {
	Soil_Temperature,                // MONICA's own: today's struct, unchanged
	^Crop2ml_Soil_Temperature,       // a generated module behind a binding (§1.3)
	^Experimental_Soil_Temperature,  // a hand-written variant
}
```

`#no_nil` makes the first variant the zero value (checked with the pinned compiler; it needs at
least 2 variants, so phase 1's one-variant union is a plain `union` until phase 2), so an
unconfigured MonicaModel selects MONICA's own implementation; `make_soil_temperature` still
initialises it as today. Dispatch in `monica_model_general_step`:

```odin
switch &impl in model.soil_temperature {
case Soil_Temperature:
	soil_temperature_step(&impl, tmin, tmax, globrad, soil_coverage, snow_depth, temperature_under_snow)
case ^Crop2ml_Soil_Temperature:
	crop2ml_soil_temperature_step(impl, model)
case ^Experimental_Soil_Temperature:
	...
}
```

Why this meets R1 and R2:

* The default branch calls the existing proc with the existing arguments in the existing order.
  No data is copied, and no arithmetic changes, so byte-identity holds by construction; the
  test only confirms it.
* A `switch` on a union per process per day costs nanoseconds, against many thousands of
  floating-point operations in the step. Union dispatch is preferable to proc pointers: the
  compiler sees every case, a missing case is a compile error, and the default case can be
  inlined.
* The other places that touch `model.soil_temperature` (init, serialization, reflective
  outputs, other processes reading soil temperature results) go through the same `switch`, or
  through the shared output of §1.2.

Same pattern as `Workstep_Data` in `odin/monica/run/workstep.odin`.

### 1.2 Shared output, and shared input only where needed

What the *rest of MONICA* reads from a process stays where it is today: the soil temperatures
live in the soil column. A non-default implementation in integrated mode writes there (scatter).
MONICA's own implementation keeps writing there directly as it does now.

For modules that don't read MonicaModel directly (generated modules, standalone mode), a process
gets an input and an output struct:

```odin
Soil_Temperature_Input :: struct {
	tmin, tmax, tavg, globrad, precip, wind, rel_humid: f64,
	julian_day: int,
	latitude, tav, tamp, albedo: f64,
	// per layer, top down: len == number of layers
	layer_thickness, bulk_density, sand, clay, silt, organic_carbon: []f64,
	field_capacity, permanent_wilting_point, saturation, soil_moisture: []f64,
	soil_coverage, lai, snow_depth, snow_water_equivalent: f64,
	et0, actual_evaporation, potential_evaporation: f64,
}

Soil_Temperature_Output :: struct {
	soil_surface_temperature: f64,
	layer_temperature:        []f64, // per MONICA layer
}
```

The field list is the union of what the C++ adapters read; trim it with the first two modules.
**Gather** (MonicaModel → input) happens only when a non-default implementation runs. Its
buffers are allocated once in `init` and reused every day, never allocated per step (R2). About
10 per-layer values for 20 layers is well under a microsecond per day.

### 1.3 One binding per generated module

A binding holds the generated Component and its five structs, and has `init(b, input)`,
`step(b, input, output)`, `destroy(b)`. It is the only code that knows both sides: unit
conversions (m → cm, kg m-3 → g cm-3, fractions → %) and the layer mapping (§1.6). Use the
generated Component's `init`, not single ModelUnit inits (the Odin Component's init applies
renamed inputs; B3 in `plan-odin-target.md`).

A hand-written variant can skip the input struct and read MonicaModel directly, like MONICA's
own implementation, if it only ever runs integrated.

### 1.4 Configuration and modes

sim.json, absent = today's behaviour:

```json
"Modules": {
  "SoilTemperature": {"impl": "DSSAT_ST_standalone", "mode": "integrated"},
  "SoilTemperatureDrivers": ["Monica_SoilTemp", "DSSAT_ST_standalone"]
}
```

* `impl` + `mode: integrated`: that implementation replaces MONICA's own (R1 doesn't apply; it's
  explicitly configured).
* `SoilTemperatureDrivers`: modules that run *alongside* (MONICA as driver). MONICA's own
  implementation still computes the soil temperature MONICA uses, and the listed modules are
  only reported. Unlike the C++ sensitivity build, nothing else in MONICA changes.
* `impl: "internal"` is allowed and must behave exactly like no configuration (tested, §3).

| Mode | Input from | Output goes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| standalone | a CSV/JSON file (weather per day, soil profile, site) | a CSV file |
| MONICA as driver | gather from MonicaModel | reported only |
| integrated | gather from MonicaModel | scatter into the soil column; MONICA's own step not run |

A name → constructor table (one per process) replaces the C++ if/else chain (R3). The extra
driver inputs the C++ branch took from `customData` and `x1…x6` become explicit: named climate
columns, or a documented `"ModuleInputs"` section in sim.json.

### 1.5 Outputs

With `plan-reflective-outputs.md`, results are reachable by path: the integrated result through
the existing soil column paths, driver results under e.g.
`modules.soil_temperature_drivers.DSSAT_ST_standalone.output.soil_surface_temperature`, their
inputs under `....input.<field>`, and raw generated state under e.g.
`....module.Dssat_St.s.srftemp` (a union segment naming a variant's type selects it). An
unconfigured module's path resolves to "not found" instead of dereferencing nil.

### 1.6 Layers

From `site_parameters` (`number_of_layers`, `layer_thickness`). The binding sizes the module before
`init` and maps:

* 1:1: DSSAT, Bioma, Stics, Simplace;
* Monica_SoilTemp: `n+2` temperature layers (ground and bottom layer appended), `n+3` for the
  secondary diagonal;
* ApsimCampbell: offset 2 (air and surface node);
* SQ: no layers, the same value for every layer.

Decided in phase 4: a module's layers are MONICA's layers, one to one. The count comes from
sim.json (`NumberOfLayers`). The thickness is passed per layer (`Input.layer_thickness`), so
bindings already handle layers of different thickness, should MONICA ever have them. A module's
extra layers (Monica_SoilTemp's ground and bottom layer, ApsimCampbell's air and surface node)
stay inside its binding, which maps them to MONICA's layers. There is no remapping between
different layer grids; a module that needs its own grid would bring that mapping in its binding.

### 1.7 Where the code lives

* `odin/monica/modules/<process>/`: the input/output structs, the bindings and their name table
  (phase 2). The union of `Monica_Model`, its dispatch and the gather are in `core` (decided in
  phase 1: `core` imports the module packages).
* `odin/amei/<package>/`: generated Crop2ML packages, never edited. `pixi run gen-amei`
  regenerates them from the pinned sources (`odin/versions.json`, `crop2ml`), and CI checks that
  regenerating changes nothing.
* Hand-written variants: next to the bindings, in their own package each.

### 1.8 State and serialization

MonicaModel state can be saved (`plan-serde.md`). Module state needs to be saved too. The
generated structs are plain data like the existing ones, so they should fit the same mechanism.
Not needed before phase 4, but the union must not make it hard: serialize the variant tag plus
its data.

---

## 2. Changes needed in PyCrop2ML's Odin target first

1. **`cr_math` for transcendental functions.** `CONVENTIONS.md` requires `support/cr_math` for
   `exp`, `log`, `log2`, `log10`, `pow`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`. Option in the
   generator (e.g. `--odin-math=<import path>`); `sqrt`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `is_nan` and
   `PI` stay `core:math`. `math.ln(x)` → `cr_math.log(x)`, `log(x, base)` →
   `cr_math.log(x) / cr_math.log(base)`.
2. **Allocator.** `make_*` and `init` take `allocator := context.allocator`, like the procs here.
3. Package names come from directory names; import with an alias. No change needed.

---

## 3. Phases

Each phase ends with a check, as in `plan-odin.md`. R1 is checked in *every* phase:
`diff_outputs.sh` byte-identical with no configuration.

**Phase 0: generator options (PyCrop2ML). Done 2026-10-23.** §2.1 and §2.2, documented in
PyCrop2ML's `doc/odin-target.md`. `CYML_ODIN_MATH` selects `cr_math`; its value is the import
path of `support/cr_math` as seen from the generated package. Allocating procs take
`allocator := context.allocator`. Check results:

* all 12 packages pass `odin check -vet`, with and without `cr_math`;
* with `cr_math`, only `sqrt`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `is_nan` and `sum` remain on `core:math`;
* the numeric comparison against the Python reference is unchanged, also with `cr_math`: the
  same 12 pass, and B9 fails as before.

**Phase 1: the mechanism, with only MONICA's own implementation.** `Soil_Temperature_Impl` with
the single variant `Soil_Temperature`, the dispatch `switch`, the sim.json section, the name
table with `"internal"`. No Crop2ML code yet. Checks:

* R1: `diff_outputs.sh` byte-identical without configuration, and with `"impl": "internal"`;
* R2: wall-clock time of the fixtures before/after, the difference within run-to-run noise
  (measure several runs; record the numbers in this file).

Done 2026-10-23. Decisions:

* The pinned compiler rejects `#no_nil` on a union with a single variant ("must have at least 2
  variants"). Until phase 2 adds the first module, `Soil_Temperature_Impl` is a plain
  `union { Soil_Temperature }` (Maybe-shaped, zero value nil). `make_monica_model` always sets
  it. Phase 2 adds `#no_nil` together with the second variant.
* Location (§1.7): the union, name table and dispatch are in `core`
  (`odin/monica/core/soil_temperature_impl.odin`). The union names `Soil_Temperature`, which
  needs `Soil_Column`, and `Monica_Model` holds the union, so a package outside `core` would
  import `core` while `core` imports it. What doesn't depend on `core` (input/output structs,
  bindings of generated modules) goes to `odin/monica/modules/soil_temperature/`, which `core`
  imports. A consequence for R3: a hand-written variant that reads `Monica_Model` directly has
  to live in `core` too. One that works on the input/output structs can be its own package.
* sim.json: `"Modules"` arrives with the rest of sim.json in `simulationParameters` and is parsed
  into `Simulation_Parameters.modules` (`odin/monica/params/modules_config.odin`). Shape errors
  (not an object, unknown mode) come from the merge. Unknown impl names come from
  `core.check_modules_config`, which `run_monica` calls before `make_monica_model`, next to the
  soil profile guard. `SoilTemperatureDrivers` is parsed but refused until phase 3. The section
  is only written back to JSON when it is configured.
* Other users of `model.soil_temperature`: the automatic sowing soil temperature average and the
  `STemp` output alias read the soil column through `soil_temperature`'s back-pointer. Both now
  read `model.soil_column` directly, which is the same memory (§1.2). `SurfTemp`
  (`soil_temperature.soil_surface_temperature`) stays. `reflectpath` unwraps the Maybe-shaped
  union, and it now also traverses general unions: a field segment is looked up in the variants
  (struct or pointer to struct, first match wins) and reads as missing while another variant is
  active (§1.5). So phase 2's `#no_nil` doesn't break output paths. Unit-tested in
  `tests/reflectpath_test.odin`.
* Reference harnesses in `odin/tests/*_ref` that step `model.soil_temperature` directly use
  `.(core.Soil_Temperature)`.

Checks:

* R1: `diff_outputs.sh` byte-identical (8 sections). Beyond the fixtures, the C++ repo's suites
  (`tests/run.py`, Hohenfinow2 and 48 muencheberg_v140, 53 CSVs) are byte-identical between the
  binaries before (566094e) and after. These include sim.json and sim+.json, which have `STemp`
  and `SurfTemp`. With `"Modules": {"SoilTemperature": {"impl": "internal", "mode":
  "integrated"}}` added, sim-min, sim-min-events2, sim-min-setvalue, sim, sim+ and sim-ser give
  output byte-identical to the runs without it. Unknown impl, unknown mode, drivers and a
  non-object section each stop the run with an error.
* R2: `hyperfine -N`, 3 warmups, 30 runs (sim.json: 15). Two rounds, the second with the binaries
  in reverse order. Linux x86_64, 48 cores, release build. Mean ± standard deviation in ms:

  | fixture | round | before | after | after − before |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | sim-min | 1 | 364 ± 14 | 360 ± 15 | −4 (−1.1 %) |
  | sim-min | 2 | 349 ± 9 | 353 ± 7 | +4 (+1.1 %) |
  | sim-min-events2 | 1 | 356 ± 17 | 358 ± 15 | +2 (+0.6 %) |
  | sim-min-events2 | 2 | 347 ± 9 | 342 ± 7 | −5 (−1.4 %) |
  | sim-min-setvalue | 1 | 267 ± 6 | 264 ± 6 | −3 (−1.1 %) |
  | sim-min-setvalue | 2 | 266 ± 5 | 267 ± 4 | +1 (+0.4 %) |
  | sim | 1 | 1975 ± 25 | 1968 ± 15 | −7 (−0.4 %) |
  | sim | 2 | 1995 ± 32 | 2019 ± 34 | +24 (+1.2 %) |

  The differences have both signs and are within one standard deviation, and the round-to-round
  drift of the same binary (sim-min before: 364 vs 349) is larger than any of them. That is
  run-to-run noise.

**Phase 2: standalone, two modules.** Input/output structs, bindings for Monica_SoilTemp and
DSSAT_ST_standalone, and `cmd/monica-module` (process + module name, input file in, CSV out).
Checks: same numbers as the generated Python code on the same input (PyCrop2ML's
`odin_reference.py` does this comparison), and Monica_SoilTemp against MONICA's own
`soil_temperature_step` on the same input. Close agreement is expected. Bit-identity only holds
where the Crop2ML source keeps MONICA's evaluation order and, after phase 0, uses `cr_math`;
where it doesn't, document the difference rather than force it.

Done 2026-10-23. What was built:

* `pixi run gen-amei` (`odinw.py gen-amei`): fetches PyCrop2ML and SoilTemperatureModels at the
  commits pinned in `odin/versions.json` (`crop2ml`) into `odin/build/crop2ml/`. Then it runs
  PyCrop2ML in its own pixi environment (its `pyproject.toml`, so none of its dependencies come
  into ours) on a copy of each listed package, targets `odin` and `py`, with
  `CYML_ODIN_MATH=../../support/cr_math`. The Odin code goes to `odin/amei/<package>/`
  (committed, never edited). The Python code stays in the build directory for the reference.
  Generation is deterministic. Both packages pass `odin check -vet`. CI (Linux pixi job)
  regenerates and fails if `amei/` changes. Instead of the `monica_amei` submodules, as §1.7 had
  it, the sources are pinned like the other third-party versions (`UPDATING_VERSIONS.md`).
* `odin/monica/modules/soil_temperature/` (package `soil_temperature`): `Input`/`Output` (§1.2,
  trimmed to what the two modules read; MONICA's units), the bindings `Monica_Soil_Temp` and
  `Dssat_St` (`init`, `step`, `destroy`), the `Module` union of their pointers, and the name
  table. It imports `params` and the `amei` packages, not `core`. `core` imports it. The gather
  for the per-run part (`core.soil_temperature_input_from_model`) is in
  `core/soil_temperature_impl.odin`, ready for phase 3.
* Binding decisions, documented in the binding files:
  * Monica_SoilTemp: the Component's `init` (it calls only the SoilTemperature unit's, as the
    C++ adapter did), damping factor 0.8, the constant soil moisture as in MONICA's own (§4).
  * DSSAT: thicknesses rounded to whole cm instead of truncated (`int(0.29 * 100)` is 28),
    `SW` set every day, albedo from MONICA's environment parameters, `TAV`/`TAMP` from
    `clim.data_accessor_calc_tamp_and_tav` (already ported, with its last-month quirk).
* `cmd/monica-module` (built with the others, also by Nix and Docker):
  `run SoilTemperature <impl> <input.json> [out.csv]`, where `impl` is a module or `internal`
  (MONICA's own `soil_temperature_step` on the same input). It also has
  `from-sim <sim.json> <input.json>`, which writes an input file from a MONICA setup: the soil
  after MONICA's pedotransfer functions, the initial moisture, and the climate. The input format
  is documented in `main.odin`. Output: CSV with 17 significant digits.
* `odin/tools/module_reference.py`: runs the generated Python on the same input, with the same
  mapping, through PyCrop2ML's `PythonReference` (`test/cyml/odin_reference.py`), and compares
  two CSVs (`--compare`). `--dynamic` derives a variant of an input with crop cover, snow (10 of
  every 30 days) and daily soil moisture between the wilting point and field capacity.
* `odin/tests/check_modules.sh` runs all of it; CI runs it on Linux.

Check results (Hohenfinow2 sim-min, 1991–1997, 2557 days × 21 values, and its dynamic variant):

| comparison | sim-min | dynamic variant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monica_SoilTemp vs MONICA's own (`internal`) | 53697 identical | 53697 identical |
| Monica_SoilTemp, Odin vs generated Python | 53697 identical | 53697 identical |
| DSSAT_ST_standalone, Odin vs generated Python | 53319 identical, 378 within 2.4e-14 | 53291 identical, 406 within 2.1e-14 |

The DSSAT differences come from `cos`/`exp`/`log`: correctly rounded in Odin (CORE-MATH), libm in
Python. Monica_SoilTemp's Crop2ML source keeps MONICA's evaluation order, so it is bit-identical
to MONICA's own. R1: `diff_outputs.sh` and the C++ suites (53 CSVs) are byte-identical. R2:
`monica-run` before/after: sim-min 373 ± 23 vs 371 ± 21 ms, sim 1975 ± 47 vs 1964 ± 26 ms.

**Phase 3: MONICA as driver.** Gather in `monica_model_general_step`, `SoilTemperatureDrivers`,
reflective outputs. Checks: R1, R2 unchanged. With drivers configured, MONICA's own outputs stay
byte-identical (drivers must not change anything), and the driver outputs are close to the C++
AMEI sensitivity build on Hohenfinow2. Last-bit differences are expected: the C++ generated code
uses `std::exp` etc., not `cr::`.

Done 2026-10-26. What was built:

* `Monica_Model.modules` (`core/soil_temperature_impl.odin`): one `Soil_Temperature_Driver` per
  `SoilTemperatureDrivers` entry (module, input, output). They sit in a map by name, for output
  paths, and in a list in sim.json order, for stepping. `check_modules_config` checks the names
  and refuses duplicates.
* Gather: the per-run input (`soil_temperature_input_from_model`) right after MONICA's own soil
  temperature is made. Not later: `make_soil_organic` moves part of the organic carbon into its
  pools, which changes the organic matter MONICA's own soil temperature has already read.
  Gathering at the end of `make_monica_model` gave a different heat capacity, about 1 %.
  `from-sim` gathers at the same point (it configures a driver). `run_monica` sets `tav`/`tamp`
  from the climate (`clim.data_accessor_calc_tamp_and_tav`), only when drivers exist. The daily
  input is gathered in `monica_model_general_step` right after MONICA's own step: the same values
  it got, and the soil moisture before today's moisture step, as in the C++ adapters. The init
  runs on the first step, as in the C++ adapters.
* Memory: module steps allocate temporaries. They go to a `mem.Dynamic_Arena` in `Modules`,
  reset after each day's drivers, because under a server's per-call arena they would otherwise
  pile up for the whole run. The bindings' state arrays are sized in init with the model's
  allocator, and resizing keeps that allocator. The generated steps of both packages only
  allocate locals (checked).
* `reflectpath`: a segment naming a union variant's type selects that variant, for raw module
  state when several variants share a field name.
* `output.csv-options.precision` (significant digits, default 6, which is the C++ formatting and
  stays byte-identical): 17 for checks that compare values exactly. NOTE(deviation), not in the
  C++.
* `odin/tests/check_drivers.py`, run by `tests/check_modules.sh` (so in CI).

Check results:

* R1: `diff_outputs.sh` and the C++ suites (53 CSVs) byte-identical without configuration.
* Drivers change nothing: sim-min, sim-min-events2 and sim-min-setvalue give byte-identical CSVs
  with both modules as drivers.
* sim-min with 17-digit output, 2557 days (316 with snow, 1961 with crop cover): the Monica_SoilTemp
  driver equals MONICA's own soil temperature exactly, in every layer and at the surface. Both
  drivers equal `monica-module` run standalone on the inputs they got (reported through
  `....input.*`), exactly. The raw state path gives the output's value.
* Against the C++ AMEI build. The sensitivity build takes its inputs from `customData` constants,
  not from MONICA, so I compared the C++ *integrated* DSSAT instead, on bare soil (sim-min without
  crops). There nothing feeds back: MONICA's water and snow balance don't read soil temperature,
  and the C++ AMEI moisture is identical with and without DSSAT. Surface temperature: equal within
  the 6 printed digits. Layers: up to 0.018 °C apart. That gap comes entirely from the AMEI
  branch's MONICA, whose soil moisture differs from master's by up to 0.036 m3 m-3; Odin's equals
  C++ master's exactly. Odin's DSSAT run standalone on the AMEI branch's moisture (the previous
  day's, as the adapter sees it) is within 0.00025 °C of the C++ AMEI DSSAT. That is the
  precision of the available outputs: moisture printed with 4 decimals, temperatures with 6.
* R2 (`hyperfine`, phase 2 vs phase 3 binary): sim-min 362 ± 8 vs 364 ± 8 ms, sim
  2066 ± 41 vs 2054 ± 34 ms. With both drivers configured: sim 2078 ± 53 ms.

**Phase 4: integrated.** Scatter into the soil column, MONICA's own step not run. Checks:
integrated Monica_SoilTemp is close to the default run (same algorithm; see phase 2 for
identity). The other modules run a full Hohenfinow2 simulation without NaN or bounds-check
panics. Layers (§1.6) are decided here.

Done 2026-10-26. What was built:

* `Soil_Temperature_Impl :: union #no_nil { Soil_Temperature, ^Soil_Temperature_Module }`. With
  two variants, `#no_nil` is possible; MONICA's own is the zero value. Every module of the
  modules table is an `impl` (integrated), without a row in `core`'s table (R3).
* `Soil_Temperature_Module` is the one struct for an integrated module and a driver (module,
  input, output). Both are made at the same point, step through the same proc on the same daily
  values, and share the scratch arena. Integrated, `soil_temperature_module_scatter` writes the
  output into the soil column: the layers' `soil_temperature` and `soil_surface_temperature`,
  which the crop module reads. MONICA's own step writes the same two.
* `SurfTemp` now reads `soil_column.soil_surface_temperature` (NOTE(deviation); MONICA's own
  sets it to the same value, so R1 holds). The C++ path read MONICA's own object, which an
  integrated module doesn't have. `STemp` already read the soil column (phase 1).
* Decisions:
  * Layers: see §1.6, one to one.
  * Monica_SoilTemp keeps MONICA's constant soil moisture (§4). Integrated, it then is exactly
    MONICA's own soil temperature, as the checks show. The actual moisture would change MONICA's
    algorithm; if wanted, that is a variant of its own, not a binding setting.

Checks (`tests/check_drivers.py`, in CI through `check_modules.sh`):

* R1: `diff_outputs.sh` and the C++ suites (53 CSVs) byte-identical without configuration.
* Monica_SoilTemp integrated: sim-min, sim-min-events2, sim-min-setvalue, sim and sim+ give
  byte-identical output (9 files), so "close to the default run" is in fact identical.
* DSSAT_ST_standalone integrated: all five run to the end, with no panic, NaN or inf. It
  changes the results through the feedback, e.g. sim.json's yields by up to about 10 %
  (6677 to 5991 kg ha-1 in one year).
* Each module integrated, with itself as a driver too: the soil column's temperatures equal the
  driver's outputs exactly, 2557 days, so the scatter is exact.
* R2: sim-min 373 ± 16 (phase 3) vs 348 ± 9 ms, sim 1976 ± 30 vs 1968 ± 41 ms. Integrated
  (information only): sim 2082 ± 99 ms with Monica_SoilTemp, 2069 ± 76 ms with DSSAT.

**Phase 5: the remaining soil temperature modules, then evapotranspiration.** One binding each.
ET scatters into `soil_moisture` like the C++ adapter (`Monica_Evapotranspiration_...cpp`, about
lines 96–118). That adapter syncs state both ways and its commit says it is "not yet working
correctly", so it comes last.

Soil temperature done 2026-10-26. What was built:

* PyCrop2ML pin moved to 5e70e28 (B12 fixed upstream), which leaves Monica_SoilTemp and
  DSSAT_ST_standalone unchanged. Seven more packages from SoilTemperatureModels: all nine with a
  C++ AMEI adapter. Not included: BiomaSurfacePartonSoilSWATHourlyPartonC (B9) and
  campbell_SoilTemp (no adapter). All pass `odin check -vet`.
* `gen-amei` now deletes the source repository's `src/odin` and `src/py` from its working copy
  before generating. Stics' committed Python had a stale `soil_tempComponent.py` with a different
  unit order next to the generated `Soil_tempComponent.py`, and the reference picked either.
* `Input` has the per-run fields the new modules need: organic carbon, sand, clay, silt, stones and
  the bare-soil `KcFactor`. The daily values are grouped as `Daily` (precipitation, irrigation,
  wind, air pressure, day length, ET0, current Kc, actual evaporation, snow depth and water
  equivalent, crop biomass, height and LAI), and `core.soil_temperature_daily` gathers them once
  per day for all modules. Timing as in the C++ adapters: before the day's soil moisture step.
* One binding file per module, after its C++ adapter. Deviations, documented in each file:
  * thicknesses in cm are rounded, not truncated (`thickness_cm`; DSSAT, EPIC, Stics);
  * ApsimCampbell: canopy height in mm (the adapter passed metres), soil albedo from MONICA (the
    adapter left it at 0);
  * Bioma: the adapter's "volumetric water content" = moisture − wilting point is kept.
* Each module's first step runs with the model's allocator, the following ones with the scratch.
  ApsimCampbell sizes state arrays lazily in its first step, so they would otherwise sit in
  memory that is reset after the day.
* `tools/module_reference.py` has a mapping per module. Parameters the binding doesn't set get
  what the generated Odin's `make_*` gives them: the default, also when it is an arithmetic
  expression (ApsimCampbell's `timestep = 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0`), otherwise zero or empty.
  PyCrop2ML's `Inputs` (in `odin_reference.py`) invents values in both cases, so ApsimCampbell's
  Python ran with a time step of 1 s. Worth fixing there too.
* `math.sqrt` is allowed besides `libc.sqrt` (CONVENTIONS.md §1): `core:math`'s is the intrinsic,
  IEEE-correctly rounded, and the generated code uses it. The convention checks skip `odin/build/`.

Evapotranspiration, 2026-10-26, on branch `crop2ml-et` (the soil temperature part is on
`simplify_copilot`).

Assessment first. In the C++ AMEI branch the module replaces exactly one call:
`SoilMoisture::fm_Evapotranspiration` inside the soil moisture step, after infiltration and
percolation, before the capillary rise. Unlike soil temperature, it changes MONICA's state (soil
moisture, surface water) and needs crop values (transpiration, remaining ET, intercepted
evaporation, gross photosynthesis). The two packages:

* Monica_Evapotranspiration: MONICA's soil-moisture ET, split into 11 Crop2ML units (radiation,
  vapour pressures, net radiation, stomata resistance, ET0, external ET0 and vapour pressure,
  potential ET, the evaporation/transpiration step). Compared with the port (= C++ master) it has
  three deliberate differences:
  1. `eReducer1` uses the current soil moisture, after infiltration. The C++ AMEI branch changed
     MONICA's own code the same way ("was wrong as within soil moisture vm_SoilMoisture got
     already updated"). Master, and so the port, still reads the moisture of the start of the day.
  2. ET0 is "unified": with a crop it is computed with the soil moisture's formula and the crop's
     stomata resistance. MONICA instead takes the crop module's ET0, whose formula differs: no
     cap of the relative shortwave radiation at 1, and its own extraterrestrial radiation.
  3. The aerodynamic term is written `rs / ra`, where MONICA has `(rs / 208) * u2`, which differs
     in the last bits.

  It has no FAO-56 dual Kc, which the port added later.
* Monica_AMEI_potential_Evapotranspiration only computes ET0 and the potential ET, from
  intermediates (vapour pressures, net radiation, stomata resistance) that MONICA has only as
  local variables, in two places. Its C++ adapter sets only the vapour pressure and, integrated,
  replaces the whole `fm_Evapotranspiration` while only setting ET0. Then evaporation and
  transpiration never leave the soil water. It also takes the crop's ET0 only *with* an external
  ET0, which looks inverted. Not usable integrated; no binding yet (as a driver it would need
  MONICA to keep those intermediates).

What was built:

* `"Modules": {"Evapotranspiration": {"impl": ...}, "EvapotranspirationDrivers": [...]}`.
  `check_modules_config` checks the names, refuses modules that can't be integrated (the table's
  `integrated` flag), and refuses an integrated module together with
  `"evapotranspiration-method": "FAO-56-Dual"`.
* `odin/monica/modules/evapotranspiration/`: `Input` (site, MONICA's soil moisture and crop module
  parameters, layers; `Daily`; the soil moisture and the crop's transpiration per layer) and
  `Output` (ET0, potential ET, net radiation, evaporation from the surface, actual E/T/ET, surface
  water, soil moisture and E/T/ET per layer). Binding `monica_et.odin` after the adapter. It also
  sets what the adapter left at 0: CO2, the crop's gross photosynthesis and carboxylation pathway,
  stomata alpha/beta, and the fixed stomata resistance without a crop (100 s m-1).
* `core/evapotranspiration_impl.odin`. `Soil_Moisture.modules` is nil without configuration, and
  then `soil_moisture_step` calls MONICA's own `evapotranspiration` unchanged (R1). Otherwise
  `evapotranspiration_with_modules` gathers the input at that point (a snapshot of soil moisture
  and surface water), runs the integrated module and scatters its output (soil column moisture,
  surface water, ET0, net radiation, E/T/ET with their layers), or MONICA's own; then the drivers
  run on the same snapshot. The scratch arena and first-step rule are shared with the soil
  temperature modules.

Check results (Hohenfinow2 sim-min, 2557 days):

* As a driver, against MONICA's own (17 digits): transpiration equal (2540 days identical, rest
  ≤ 3e-5 mm, with a crop: the remaining-ET path); evaporation from surface water equal; ET0
  without a crop within 1.8e-15; soil evaporation different on about 700 days by up to 3.15 mm.
  With the C++ AMEI branch's `eReducer1` patched into MONICA's own (a one-off experiment, not
  committed), soil evaporation is equal within 9e-16. ET0 with a crop differs by up to 1.22 mm
  (difference 2).
* Integrated, against MONICA's default: everything runs, the yields within about 0.2 % (e.g.
  7589 vs 7600 kg ha-1). Against MONICA with the patched `eReducer1`: 34 of 48651 output numbers
  differ, all of them `ETa/ETc`, the only output that uses the reported ET0. So the integrated
  module is MONICA's own ET plus differences 1 and 2.
* `tests/check_drivers.py`: ET drivers change nothing (5 sims byte-identical); integrated, all 5
  run without NaN or inf; integrated with itself as a driver, MONICA's E/T/ET0 (and layers) equal
  the module's exactly.
* R1: `diff_outputs.sh` and the C++ suites byte-identical. R2: sim-min 357 ± 8 vs 354 ± 8 ms, sim
  2005 ± 24 vs 2011 ± 21 ms; integrated ET sim 1985 ± 19 ms.
* Not done: a Python reference for the ET packages (`module_reference.py`). The comparison
  against MONICA's own code above is the stronger check here.

**Phase 6: a second process as a module (optional, proves R3).** E.g. move evapotranspiration's
internal code behind its own union like soil temperature in phase 1, then write a small
hand-written variant as the "PhD student" test case. Check: R1, R2, and that the variant needed
only its package, one union entry and one table row.

## 4. Known issues in the modules (fix in the Crop2ML packages, not in bindings)

* MONICA evapotranspiration, `radiation.pyx` lines 41–45 and `stomata_resistance.pyx` line 5:
  a result stays unassigned with the default input (B10/B11 in `plan-odin-target.md`). In Odin
  it silently becomes 0.0.
* BiomaSurfacePartonSoilSWATHourlyPartonC can't run (B9).
* Unit order in compositions (B12): fixed upstream (PyCrop2ML 4683b96, pinned from phase 5).
* ApsimCampbell's cpp2 code in `monica_amei` was hand-edited; the Odin code is regenerated from
  the Crop2ML sources, so compare behaviour, not code.
* Monica_SoilTemp's C++ adapter uses a constant soil moisture per layer, `pwp + awc * (fc - pwp)`
  with `awc = 0.25`. MONICA's own soil temperature uses a different constant:
  `SoilTemperatureParameters.SoilMoisture`, 0.25 m3 m-3 in every layer (`soil_temperature.odin`,
  `soil_moisture_const`). The other modules get the actual moisture per layer. The Odin binding
  uses MONICA's own constant (phase 2), which makes Monica_SoilTemp bit-identical to MONICA's own
  soil temperature. Decide in phase 4 whether integrated mode should get the actual moisture.
* ApsimCampbell's adapter sets both Eo and Eos to the potential ET (with a `!!!` comment
  questioning it), and Simplace's sets `iRAIN = precip` "so that no snowcover will build up".
  Adapter decisions: carry them into the bindings explicitly, document them, revisit later.
* Stics_soil_temperature: from about 50 cm down, every layer has the same temperature, which
  follows the season without damping or lag. So in summer the deep layers are warmer than the
  surface (Hohenfinow2, 15 July 1992: 18.7 °C at 50–200 cm, 15.6 °C at the surface). The
  generated Python and the C++ AMEI build agree, so it is the module's behaviour with MONICA's
  20 × 10 cm profile, not a binding error. Check against STICS.
* Simplace_Soil_Temperature declares `cInitialSnowWaterContent` in percent; the module computes
  with mm, which is what the adapter and the binding pass.
* Monica_Evapotranspiration, the evapotranspiration unit: without a crop and with snow, it doesn't
  reset `transpiration[i]` (MONICA sets it to 0). So the state's value from the last crop day
  would be counted again. It didn't happen on Hohenfinow2 (transpiration equal on every day).
* Monica_Evapotranspiration's ET0 with a crop is the soil moisture's formula, not the crop
  module's (phase 5, difference 2). Decide which one MONICA should have and use it in both.
